shared_contexts.heading: Format and Semantics of Instruction Descriptions
shared_contexts.quotation_rendered_text: Format and Semantics of Instruction Descriptions 9.1. This section describes each PTX instruction. In addition to the name and the format of the instruction, the semantics are described, followed by some examples that attempt to show several possible instantiations of the instruction.

shared_contexts.heading: Predicated Execution
shared_contexts.quotation_rendered_text: In PTX, predicate registers are virtual and have .pred as the type specifier. So, predicate registers can be declared as .reg .pred p, q, r; All instructions have an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction. The syntax to specify conditional execution is to prefix an instruction with @{!}p, where p is a predicate variable, optionally negated. Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally.
shared_contexts.role: Context for predicate-type variables and optional guard predicates.

shared_contexts.heading: Register State Space
shared_contexts.quotation_rendered_text: Registers (.reg state space) are fast storage locations... Registers may be typed ... Register size is restricted; aside from predicate registers which are 1-bit, scalar registers have a width of 8-, 16-, 32-, 64-, or 128-bits...
